lines.text: Today you will build forms with boxes to type in, menus to choose from and buttons to press.
A form is a group of boxes, menus and buttons that ask the visitor questions.
The form tag wraps all of them together.
Sign-up pages, quizzes and search bars are all forms.
The input tag makes a box, and its type decides what kind.
Type text is for words, number is for numbers, and checkbox is a tick box.
A textarea is a big box for longer answers, and select makes a drop-down menu.
A label tells people what to type in a box.
Its for part must match the input’s id.
Then screen readers read the label aloud, and clicking the label jumps into the box.
The button tag makes something on the page you can press.
Write clear words on it, like Send feedback, not just Click.
Next lesson, JavaScript will make our buttons actually do things.
Our practice forms in this course send nothing anywhere.
Even so, never build a form that asks for phone numbers, addresses, passwords or ID numbers.
Real websites need a parent’s and the school’s permission to collect personal details.
The label’s for matches the input’s id, so they are joined together.
Click the words and the cursor jumps into the box, which helps everyone.
Changing the type changes the kind of box the browser draws.
A textarea is for long answers, and select makes a drop-down menu of options.
The button tag makes something you can press.
For now it does nothing, and next lesson JavaScript will bring it to life.
Display block puts each label on its own line, so the form is easy to follow.
Padding makes boxes bigger and easier to tap on a phone.
Look closely at the spelling of for and id.
One says colour and the other says color, so they do not match and are not joined.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
